A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OWL study. Their main texts, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison, including matching material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations on three probing tasks, including multilingual, audio, perturbation, and quantization results.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds training-corpus overlap counts, OLMo subset evaluations, and further performance breakdowns.

M1.justification: The three probing procedures, prompts, outputs, and audio and quantization adaptations remain unchanged. The new corpus audit and expanded reporting do not introduce a new probing algorithm or model component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same OWL book collection, ten languages, English audio, three probing tasks, and 2024 book controls. The corpus-overlap audit examines existing OWL passages and supports subset selection within this retained coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated GPT-4o, LLaMA, Qwen, OLMo-2, and EuroLLM models remain the same, including audio and quantized variants. The new analyses reuse these models; Table 13's additional corpus-index names do not represent new evaluated model comparators.

E3.justification: v2 adds evaluation conditioned on training exposure: OLMo is assessed on passages classified as present in English training data while corresponding translations were not found (Section 4, Figures 7–8). Table 13 introduces the matching-span criterion and exclusion of unclear cases, substantially extending the evaluation controls.

E4.justification: The new corpus-overlap audit and OLMo subset analysis directly investigate the training-exposure premise underlying cross-lingual transfer. Appendix F also extends book-level analysis to prefix probing with and without character names, while Figure 23 adds language-specific character-removal breakdowns.

E5.justification: Both versions report model performance as point estimates without repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The dataset dispersion statistics in Table 2 are unchanged.

E6.justification: Existing result tables and chart values are retained. Substantial new entries include corpus-match counts, OLMo subset results, and language- and book-level breakdowns. For example, Figure 7 newly reports OLMo-2-13B direct-probing accuracy of 62.9%, 48.7%, and 33.9% on English, official translations, and unseen translations within the selected subset.

T1.justification: Neither version develops theoretical propositions, proofs, or mathematical derivations. The newly documented matching and filtering rules are operational experimental criteria.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows consistent cross-lingual recall to 'some LLMs' and frames perturbation robustness as performance remaining above chance. The conclusion elevates character names as a strong recall signal. The dataset contribution and three-task research agenda remain intact.

C2.justification: v2 substantially qualifies interpretation through its new training-data limitation and discussion of private translations, possible non-English OLMo training text, and audiobook exposure. Section 4 explicitly recognizes weak verbatim recall relative to 2024 controls and removes the stronger inference that reliance on lexical cues implies a lack of deep understanding.

D1.justification: v2 specifies the asymmetric character-length filter in Section 2 and documents the Infini-gram index and matching rule for the new audit. It also clarifies which passages contain character names and corrects prose counts to agree with existing tables. These disclosures do not establish changes to the original data-processing implementation.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds discussion of Prashanth et al. (2025) and Zhang et al. (2025), and Liu et al. (2024) is newly cited for Infini-gram. The broader positioning relative to earlier memorization probes and cross-lingual transfer research remains stable.

P1.justification: The abstract and results receive clarity and qualification edits, character-name terminology is standardized, and explanatory passages are added about literary data and training exposure. The main section sequence and Appendix A–F organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The results displays are substantially reorganized: v1 Figures 3, 8, and 9 move to the appendix as v2 Figures 18–20. v2 adds two main-text OLMo plots, three appendix heatmaps, and the corpus-search table, while relocating several existing tables. Existing chart graphics are retained.

improvement.justification: The corpus audit and OLMo subset results partly address v1's reliance on assumed training exposure, while the revised discussion better calibrates claims about recall and transfer. The gain is limited: Table 13 classifies exposure using a matching span of at most 20 words, which does not establish exposure to an entire passage.
